drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find our proposed revisions to the mutual NDA. We have clarified the confidentiality and permitted-use obligations, added customary exceptions and compelled-disclosure procedures, and addressed return of information and survival. The agreement remains mutual and does not commit either party to a transaction. Please let us know if these revisions are acceptable.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction (the Purpose). Each party may disclose Confidential Information to the other in connection with the Purpose. Neither party is required to disclose information or proceed with any transaction, and no obligation to consummate a transaction arises unless a definitive agreement is executed by both parties.

2. CONFIDENTIALITY AND PERMITTED USE. In consideration of their mutual undertakings, each party receiving information (the Receiving Party) shall use the disclosing party's (the Disclosing Party's) Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it using at least reasonable care. Confidential Information means nonpublic information disclosed in any form in connection with the Purpose that is identified as confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential, including analyses derived from it and the existence and status of discussions. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information only to its personnel, affiliates and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality duties at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for their compliance. Confidential Information excludes information the Receiving Party can demonstrate was lawfully known to it without restriction before disclosure, becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, is lawfully received from a third party without confidentiality restrictions, or is independently developed without use of Confidential Information. If disclosure is legally compelled, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt advance notice, reasonably cooperate at the Disclosing Party's expense in seeking protection, and disclose only the portion legally required. Upon written request, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy Confidential Information, except copies required by law, professional retention obligations or routine automated backups; retained information remains subject to this Agreement. No intellectual property rights are transferred or licensed except the limited right to use information for the Purpose.

3. TERM AND SURVIVAL. This Agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and remains in effect for twenty-four months, unless either party terminates it earlier by written notice. Confidentiality and use restrictions survive for three years after expiration or termination; for information constituting a trade secret under applicable law, those restrictions continue for so long as it remains a trade secret. Termination does not affect rights arising from a prior breach.

4. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause harm for which damages alone are inadequate. The Disclosing Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief, subject to applicable law, in addition to damages and any other available remedies.

Please also require return or destruction within 30 days of written request, written certification on request, and no access to retained copies except for legally required compliance or bona fide backup recovery, with all retained information remaining protected.

In consideration of their mutual undertakings, each party receiving information (the Receiving Party) shall use the disclosing party's (the Disclosing Party's) Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it using at least reasonable care. Confidential Information means nonpublic information disclosed in any form in connection with the Purpose that is identified as confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential, including analyses derived from it and the existence and status of discussions. If disclosure is legally compelled, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt advance notice, reasonably cooperate at the Disclosing Party's expense in seeking protection, and disclose only the portion legally required. Upon becoming aware of any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall promptly notify the Disclosing Party and reasonably cooperate with it to contain and mitigate the unauthorized use or disclosure. Within 30 days after receipt of a written request from the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy Confidential Information, including copies held by persons to whom it disclosed that information, except copies required by law, professional retention obligations or routine automated backups. Upon request, the Receiving Party shall provide written certification of compliance with these return or destruction obligations, identifying the categories of any copies retained under these exceptions. Retained copies may not be accessed except for legally required compliance or bona fide backup recovery, and all retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality and permitted-use obligations of this Agreement for so long as it is retained, notwithstanding Section 3. Any Confidential Information restored through backup recovery shall remain protected and shall promptly be returned, destroyed or isolated from access except as permitted under the foregoing retention exceptions. No intellectual property rights are transferred or licensed except the limited right to use information for the Purpose.
